title: Re-Run the Accounts Task
subtitle: A retry must reuse, not duplicate
scenario: The accounts task ran yesterday but timed out mid-way - it is unclear whether the account was created. You re-run it. This time the identity check FINDS an existing account for H-4022. The idempotency rule earns its keep: reuse it, do not create a second one.
input: Task: accounts for hire H-4022, re-run after a timeout. Identity store lookup for H-4022: an existing account (acct-4022) IS found from the interrupted first run. Rule: check first; if one exists, REUSE it and record action = reused. Never create a second account.
instructions: Record the taskId and that an existing account was found (existingFound = true).
Because one exists, set action to reused and record the existing accountId.
Set the final state to done.
Return one valid JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build one JSON accounts re-run result: taskId, existingFound (boolean true), action (reused), accountId (acct-4022), state (done). An existing account was found, so reuse it - do not create a second.
successMessage: Account reused. The retry converged to one account - idempotency held.
editorHelper: Found one? Reuse it. That is what makes a retry safe.

intro.heading: Before you retry: converge, do not duplicate

sections.title: Retries are normal
sections.body: A timeout mid-task is routine in real provisioning. The question is not 'did it run twice?' but 'did running twice do harm?'. Idempotency is the answer that makes retries safe.

sections.title: The check pays off now
sections.body: In the easy run, existingFound was false and you created. Here it is true, so you reuse. Same rule, opposite branch - the check-then-create discipline is what prevents a duplicate.

sections.title: One account, always
sections.body: Whether the task runs once or five times, the hire ends with exactly one account. That convergence is the whole point; two accounts would break offboarding and audit.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: An accounts result showing a reused account - proof the retry was safe. The tracker reads it the same as a created one: done.

takeaway.heading: Account reused
points: You re-ran the task and found an existing account.
Because one existed, you reused it - action reused, not a second create.
The retry converged to exactly one account: idempotency held.
The tracker reads a reused account the same as a created one: done.
The workflow can now retry provisioning safely without duplicating accounts.
